lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: This is Waystation Nine CB, ninety seven point four. Channel's open, coffee's hot, and the roads go every which way.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Waystation Nine. The truck stop at the crossroads of everywhere. Big Rosalind on dispatch.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Waystation Nine CB. Up, down or sideways, somebody's driving it tonight.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Breaker, breaker. You're listening to Waystation Nine.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: That's right, Mongoose. They are.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Waystation Nine CB. Fragile loads, long hauls, and strong opinions about the sideways road.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Morning, drivers. Waystation Nine. Coffee's on, the Up Road's awake, and the sideways road is pretending not to be.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Mongoose, what are you hauling tonight?

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Same as always, Rosalind. Forty tonne of Tuesday, northbound.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Fragile?

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Says so on the side. Hit a pothole on the Down Road last month, and a whole town got two Tuesdays. Nobody was happy.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Drive careful, Mongoose.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Rosalind, you seen Grandma Diesel tonight?

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Seen her? She came through here four minutes ago doing a hundred and ten. Knitting.

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Hundred and twelve, dear. And it's a cardigan.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: She's... she's behind me, Rosalind.

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Not any more, pet.

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Rosalind, I'll need a wide berth on the Up Road. I've got a thunderstorm in the back, and it's getting restless.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: How restless?

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Rattling the doors since the county line. I've put the radio on for it. It likes the slow ones.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Copy that. All drivers, Grandma Diesel's coming through with weather. Pull over and put your hoods up.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: You know, Rosalind, I been driving this stretch since it was a river.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: I know, Mongoose.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Used to row it. Had a little boat. Then one spring the water just got up and left, and they paved it over, and I thought, well. I know the way.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: You still steer round the rocks.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Rocks are still there, Rosalind. You just can't see them.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: A word about the sideways road. I don't trust it. It knows where you're going before you do, and it gets there first, and it waits for you.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Drivers, if you must take the sideways road: eyes front, doors locked, and don't, whatever you do, let it choose the radio station.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: All drivers, oversized load on the Down Road tonight. Forty tonne of compost, bound for Gristwick. For one marrow.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: One marrow, Rosalind?

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: One marrow. Second load this week. It's got its own postcode, Mongoose. It eats well.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Copy. I'll pull in and let it by.

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Rosalind, I've dropped that load of fog off at the shoegaze place.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: How'd it go?

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Lovely boy on the stage. Mumbled at me for ten minutes. I agreed with everything.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Everybody does, Grandma.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: And the Nightjar's on the channel again. Night operator, we can see your running lights over the crossroads.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: You want coffee, you'll have to come down. We don't deliver up. Well. Grandma Diesel does. But she charges.

clips.title: Relay Four on the Long Range

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Rosalind, I keep picking up a fella on the long range. Teodor. Relay Four. Asking if anybody can hear him.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: We hear him, Mongoose. Everybody does. Say hello.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Teodor, this is Midnight Mongoose, on the old river road. We hear you, friend. Ten four.

lines.speaker: The New Guy
lines.text: Uh. Waystation Nine, this is... um. This is the new guy.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Evening, new guy. Got a handle yet?

lines.speaker: The New Guy
lines.text: Not yet. I was thinking... Thunder Hawk?

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: The New Guy
lines.text: Night Wolf?

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: The New Guy
lines.text: What about...

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: You don't pick your handle, sweetheart. The road picks it. Just drive.

clips.title: The New Guy Takes the Sideways Road

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: New guy, what's your twenty?

lines.speaker: The New Guy
lines.text: I took the sideways road, Rosalind. I think... I think I'm in last Thursday.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: I told you about the sideways road.

lines.speaker: The New Guy
lines.text: You did.

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Welcome to the network, Thursday.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: There it is. The road's picked it. That's your handle now. Thursday.

lines.speaker: Thursday
lines.text: ...Copy that.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Thursday, what are you hauling?

lines.speaker: Thursday
lines.text: First fragile load, Rosalind. A whole crate of first impressions.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Steady with those. You only get the one go.

lines.speaker: Thursday
lines.text: Copy that. Thursday out.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Listen to him. Thursday out. Proud of you, kid.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Road report, from Waystation Nine dispatch. Here's how the roads are feeling.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Time for the road report. Pens out, drivers. Big Rosalind, on the map.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: The Up Road. Steady climb, good surface, light traffic. Some icing near the top, where it's never once been warm.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Keep it under fifty, and say something nice to it as you pass. It's been a bit low lately.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: The Down Road is moving well, southbound. Northbound is also moving well, but it's also going down.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Don't ask. Just enjoy it.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: The sideways road. I won't tell you how it's doing, because it'll hear me, and it'll take it personally.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: I will say there's a three mile tailback of drivers who took it to save time, and are now in last week. Take the long way.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: The Loop is running smooth, clockwise. If you've been on the Loop more than a day, you'll be passing the diner every forty minutes.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Wave at Dolores. She'll wave back. She always does.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: The old river road. Dry, as it has been for a hundred years, but drivers report the feeling of a current near the old bridge.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Midnight Mongoose says steer left of the middle. Do as Mongoose says.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Weather on the network. Grandma Diesel was hauling a thunderstorm eastbound, and it's got loose.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Expect rain on the Up Road, a short hailstorm at the junction, and one very confused rainbow on the sideways road, pointing the wrong way.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: That's the road report. Drive careful, drink your coffee, and if the road talks back, don't argue.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: That's your roads. Waystation Nine dispatch, standing by. Keep the shiny side up.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: This is the Graveyard Shift, on Waystation Nine CB. Coffee's black, the roads are dark, and every driver out there is wide awake. Talk to me.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Rosalind, you still up?

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: I'm always up, Mongoose.

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: Me too. Road's real quiet. Just me, the headlights, and a fox that's been running alongside me for ten miles.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Is he keeping up?

lines.speaker: Midnight Mongoose
lines.text: He's winning.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Three in the morning on the network. Long stretches, no lights, and the radio for company.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: If you're out there and you're tired, pull in. I'll leave the light on. I always do.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Morning, drivers. This is the Dawn Run. Night convoy's pulling in, day convoy's heading out. Mind the lot. Bacon's on.

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Morning, Rosalind. Coming in off the Up Road. Delivered a sunrise to the eastern counties.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: How'd it go?

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Bit pink. They liked it.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Bacon report. Dolores has done four hundred rashers this morning, and they're all gone. Grandma Diesel had a hundred of them.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: She says it's for the drive. She's eighty four. I'm not arguing.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Evening, all. This is Supper at the Crossroads. Pull in, pull up a stool, and let's talk about anything but the sideways road.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Dolores says the coffee's fresh. Dolores has said the coffee's fresh every night since this place opened, and Dolores has never once lied to a driver.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: So either the coffee's fresh, or time works different in that pot. Either way, it's very good coffee. Pull in.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Supper chatter. Somebody at the counter says the sideways road took him past his own house, and his own self was in the window, waving.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: I don't want to hear it. Nobody wants to hear it. Eat your pie.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Halloween on the network. Drivers, if somebody thumbs a ride on the Down Road, and they tell you they've been waiting since nineteen fifty eight, give them a lift.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: They're harmless. Very polite. They tip in old coins. Just don't take the sideways road with them in the cab. They don't like it either.

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Rosalind, I'm running a full moon out to the hill country for the thirty first.

lines.speaker: Big Rosalind
lines.text: Wide load?

lines.speaker: Grandma Diesel
lines.text: Widest there is, dear. Tell the drivers, if they see a big orange light coming up behind them, that's just me and the moon. Don't howl. It only encourages it.
